scope: Sargent and Stachurski, Dynamic Programming, Volume 2 (General States), Chapter 8: Additional Applications. Job search in L1 with Markov offers (Propositions 8.1.1-8.1.2, Exercises 8.1.1-8.1.3, 8.1.14-8.1.20), bounded offers and continuity (Exercises 8.1.4-8.1.5, with a counterexample to Exercise 8.1.4 for policy operators), continuation values, the reservation wage and the FDP of Section 8.1.2.2 via Theorem 5.2.13 (Exercises 8.1.6-8.1.7, 8.1.9-8.1.13, Example 8.1.1, Proposition A.5.20, first order stochastic dominance and mean-preserving spreads), persistent and transient shocks (Exercises 8.1.21-8.1.24); nonlinear discounting and Koopmans-type power-mean search via Du's theorem (Exercises 8.2.1-8.2.5, Section 8.2.2); job separation (Exercises 8.2.12-8.2.13, Proposition 8.2.2); job search with learning (Exercises 8.2.6-8.2.11, Proposition 8.2.1, Proposition A.5.34); Coase meets Bellman: negative discounting and the production chain (Exercises 8.3.1-8.3.3, Lemmas 8.3.3-8.3.5, Theorem 8.3.6, Definition 8.3.1, Propositions 8.3.1-8.3.2); optimal harvests via factorization (Exercise 8.3.4, Section 8.3.2.2); the stochastic growth model (Exercises 8.3.5-8.3.8 with a counterexample to Exercise 8.3.6, Proposition 8.3.7, Lemma 8.3.8), the envelope condition by the Clausen-Strub differentiable sandwich (Proposition 8.3.9 corrected, Corollary 8.3.10) and the Euler equation (Exercises 8.3.9-8.3.10, the comparison step of Exercise 8.3.12); with the earlier chapters' ADP, Banach lattice, FDP and RDP theory restated.
source: Thomas J. Sargent and John Stachurski, Dynamic Programming, Volume 2: General States, Chapter 8, pp. 247-293, with the Appendix A results used there.
